chunks: From him, from Abu Muhammad al-Madaini, from A'iz ibn Habib, the seller of al-Harawi, who said: Isa ibn Zayd narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

"The child has his teeth cut (circumcised) at seven, and is commanded to perform prayer at nine, and they are separated from each other in sleeping quarters at ten, and he experiences seminal emission at fourteen, and the end of his height is at twenty-one, and the end of his intellect is at twenty-eight, except for experience."

key_terms.مُنْتَهَى طُولِهِ: The end of his height (physical maturity)
key_terms.مُنْتَهَى عَقْلِهِ: The end of his intellect (mental maturity)
key_terms.يُفْرَقُ بَيْنَهُمْ: They are separated (referring to sleeping arrangements)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific ages for a child's physical and legal milestones in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, narrating from Imam Ali, establishes the foundational timeline for a child's physical and legal maturation in Shia fiqh, distinguishing between biological signs like puberty (ihtilam) and social-legal responsibilities such as prayer (salat). The inclusion of 'except through experience' (illa al-tajribat) at the end highlights the scholarly recognition that these ages are general guidelines subject to individual variation, a nuance critical in deriving rulings on maturity (bulugh) and sanity (aql).
